macro_context.market_sentiment: Markets are at or near all-time highs but pulled back modestly on May 7 (S&P 500 -0.38% to 7,337, Nasdaq -0.13%, DJIA -0.63%) as Iran declared the US had violated their ceasefire. The prior three sessions saw record closes driven by hopes for Iran peace talks; Paul Tudor Jones sees the AI-fueled bull market continuing for another 1-2 years.
macro_context.fed_outlook: Fed held rates at 3.50%-3.75% at the April 29, 2026 FOMC meeting in a contentious 8-4 split — the most dissent since Oct 1992. Markets price zero cuts in 2026 and one 25bp cut in December 2027. Inflation remains elevated partly due to Middle East energy price surge from the Iran War.
macro_context.geopolitical: The Iran War is the dominant risk: disrupting global energy markets and shipping routes, threatening the Strait of Hormuz, and pushing global inflation higher. IMF projects only 3.1% global growth and 4.4% headline inflation in 2026 base case. Despite this, US/Japan/South Korea equity markets have reached all-time highs, suggesting investor complacency. US military action against Iran continues, with Iran accusing US of ceasefire violations on May 7.
key_events: Iran-US ceasefire breakdown — headline risk for energy prices and risk sentiment
Fed transition: Powell stepping down as chair, policy continuity uncertain
2026 FIFA World Cup approaching — athletic apparel/footwear demand catalyst
Ongoing tariff environment weighing on consumer goods importers
IMF global growth downgrade to 3.1% for 2026 on war disruption

ticker_news.headline: Nike down 32% YTD and 65% over 3 years; under EEOC investigation for discrimination; pursuing 'Win Now' restructuring strategy
ticker_news.source: The Motley Fool / The Globe and Mail, May 6, 2026

ticker_news.headline: Nike's 65% 3-year plunge could lead to 41% upside today — analysts see mean-reversion opportunity at current ~$44 price
NKE stock gains premarket on $0.41/share quarterly dividend declaration, signaling management confidence in cash flow
Nike fiscal Q3 2026 revenue fell 2.7% YoY; net profit margin shrank to 4.8%; Converse revenue down ~35%; Greater China weakness continues
Nike has conducted two rounds of layoffs in 2026, cutting approximately 14,000 employees in first four months of the year

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: Heavy wave of downgrades in Q1-Q2 2026: Piper Sandler to Neutral (PT $50), CICC to Market Perform (PT $58), DA Davidson to Neutral (PT $46), Citi to Neutral (PT $53), Needham to Hold (Jan), Bank of America neutral at $55, Stifel hold at $56, Telsey PT cut to $55. Last upgrade was Barclays raising PT to $73 on March 11, 2026. Current breakdown per MarketBeat: 19 Buy, 16 Hold, 1 Sell — consensus 'Moderate Buy' with avg PT ~$63.25. Range: $46–$90. Stock trades ~$44, implying ~41% upside to consensus.

competitor_activity: Adidas is outperforming Nike heading into the 2026 World Cup, capitalizing on the Samba/Gazelle lifestyle shoe trend and growing market share in running and lifestyle. Adidas CEO Gulden has hit 4-year turnaround goals in 3 years. Hoka (Deckers) and On Running continue to gain share in performance running — a category where Nike's running sales did jump 20%+ in Q3 but from a low base. Under Armour is restructuring (cut Steph Curry deal, saving ~$45-50M) and fighting for relevance. Lululemon and Anta also gaining share from Nike in athleisure and China respectively. Nike is losing market share broadly across geographies and categories.
earnings_info: Next earnings: fiscal Q4 2026, estimated June 25, 2026 after market close (no official date yet confirmed). Most recent quarter (fiscal Q3 2026, ended Feb 28): EPS $0.35, revenue $11.28B (down 2.7% YoY) — fourth consecutive beat vs. estimates. Guidance implies 2-4% sales decline for Q4 due to continued weakness in Greater China and Converse. EPS estimate for FY2026 has been revised downward across the Street following Q3 guidance.
